Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Marie-Louise-Victoire marquise de La Rochejaquelein (author, Wikidata Q462516), died 1857; Amable-Guillaume-Prosper Brugière Barante (editor, Wikidata Q2988452), died 1866. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("La Rochejaquelein, Marie-Louise-Victoire marquise de, 1772-1857; Barante, Amable-Guillaume-Prosper Brugière, baron de, 1782-1866 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Mémoires de Madame la marquise de Bonchamps : rédigés par Mme la comtesse de Genlis, suivis des pièces justificatives, Paris, Baudouin frères, 1823, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_KLfvK-XYksEC. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 75%, 81%, 81% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Amable-Guillaume-Prosper Brugière Barante, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
